vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Good news — this is something you (or anyone on your team) can check and fix yourself in about 10 minutes, no developer required, though a web developer or your website host/platform support can help if you're not comfortable editing files.

## How to check it yourself

**1. Look at your robots.txt file**
Type `yoursite.com/robots.txt` into a browser. Type your domain followed by /robots.txt into a browser and read the User-agent blocks that load. A block naming an AI bot with a "Disallow: /" line beneath it means that bot is locked out. If nothing appears at all, your site most likely has no robots.txt file, which usually means every bot, AI or otherwise, has open access by default.

**2. Use a free automated checker (faster than reading manually)**
Several free tools will scan your site in seconds and tell you exactly which AI crawlers are blocked:
- **365i AI Bot Checker** – Free AI crawler checker: test if GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and 11 more can crawl your site. Checks robots.txt, server blocks, noindex and nosnippet.
- **MRS Digital AI Crawler Access Checker** – lets you see whether popular AI crawlers such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot can reach your website's pages.
- **LLM Pulse Robots.txt Checker** – See if GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, and Google-Extended can crawl your site, with line-by-line analysis.
- **RankPrompt** and **Recomaze** offer similar free scans.

These go beyond just reading the file — they fetch your homepage once as a normal browser, then once as each bot, and compare, which catches blocks happening at the server/hosting level that robots.txt alone won't show.

## Who can actually fix it

- **You, directly** — if your site is WordPress or similar, check SEO plugins. With Rank Math: go to Rank Math > General Settings > Edit robots.txt and add the AI crawler rules. With Yoast: go to Yoast > Tools > File Editor > robots.txt. Also some security plugins (Wordfence, Sucuri, iThemes) add crawler blocks — check your plugin settings.
- **Your web host or hosting support** — if a plugin is generating that file, your edit may not stick, and the next time the plugin saves its settings the block comes back — check your SEO plugin first, then anything security or firewall related, then your CDN dashboard. The 365i tool specifically mentions it will write the fix message for your hosting company so you can just forward it to support.
- **A web developer or SEO freelancer** — if you want someone else to handle the robots.txt edit and verify it's live.

## The fix (once you know what's blocked)

The recommended robots.txt setup to allow AI crawlers looks like this:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /
```

If your robots.txt has a blanket User-agent: * / Disallow: / rule, you'll need to either remove it or add explicit Allow rules for each AI crawler above it (specific user-agent rules take precedence over the wildcard).

**Bottom line:** Run your site through one of the free checkers above first — it'll tell you exactly what's blocked. If it's just a robots.txt edit, you can do it yourself or hand it to whoever manages your site's backend/hosting.
